suggestions.title: 1. MDMA: what "too late for an easy fix" means, and low sodium in the seizure line
suggestions.what: Two places in your MDMA paragraph. "(sodium might be too low and it could be too late for an easy fix)" becomes "(sodium might be too low by then for even an electrolyte drink to fix, so don't give them any more to drink)". "A seizure or collapse can result from low potassium," becomes "A seizure or collapse can result from low sodium or potassium,". Nothing else changes.
suggestions.tested: Your version read [Human High 132](https://www.pangram.com/history/c45651d9-f45e-4f3e-8496-f340eae874b0); with the two fixes, [Human Written, 0% AI, one window Human High](https://www.pangram.com/history/e1cf44d8-f5fe-4a33-98ac-24780393acd7) over all 142 words.
suggestions.why: Your question, whether to keep giving electrolytes while calling medics: no, nothing more to drink once those signs show. Electrolyte and sports drinks carry far less salt than blood, so drinking more of them still thins it; the wilderness-medicine guidelines on low sodium from overdrinking name water and sports drinks as the cause and restrict fluids once it's suspected, and hospitals treat it with fluid restriction or a concentrated salt drip (for MDMA too). Vomiting means a drink won't stay down, and confusion makes choking a risk. "Too late for an easy fix" meant that, but it reads as "nothing can be done". And low sodium, not potassium, is what most often brings the seizures in MDMA cases; very low potassium brings weakness and heart rhythm trouble, which is how it can bring a collapse.
suggestions.stays: Every other word of your paragraph, and your sipping line before the signs, which is for before any of them show.
suggestions.deciding: Approve puts both in. Revise if you'd say them your way. The fresh readers also asked two things, not changed: the seizure line names causes but no action (your "The following indicators would justify calling medics:" covers it), and "like my second wife had" is your story from the paragraph before.
suggestions.advice_note: Approve: both hold up against the sources, and the paragraph still reads Human High.

edits.before: Once their jaw tenses, that should be their last dose of MDMA, so get them to slow down and cool off. If they drink a lot of plain water, even a single normal MDMA dose raises the risk of their sodium dropping too low, so have them sip an electrolyte drink when they're thirsty instead. The following indicators would justify calling medics: If their confusion or headache worsens, or vomiting won't stop (sodium might be too low and it could be too late for an easy fix). If their muscles keep getting weaker or their heart palpitations keep getting stronger, that could be from dangerously low potassium, like my second wife had. A seizure or collapse can result from low potassium, and can also come from overheating or MDMA toxicity.
edits.after: Once their jaw tenses, that should be their last dose of MDMA, so get them to slow down and cool off. If they drink a lot of plain water, even a single normal MDMA dose raises the risk of their sodium dropping too low, so have them sip an electrolyte drink when they're thirsty instead. The following indicators would justify calling medics: If their confusion or headache worsens, or vomiting won't stop (sodium might be too low by then for even an electrolyte drink to fix, so don't give them any more to drink). If their muscles keep getting weaker or their heart palpitations keep getting stronger, that could be from dangerously low potassium, like my second wife had. A seizure or collapse can result from low sodium or potassium, and can also come from overheating or MDMA toxicity.
